english: Let $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and let $I_A=\{(a,a):a\in A\}$ denote the identity relation on $A$. For a relation $R$ on $A$, let $R^{-1}$ denote its inverse. Then the number of relations $R$ on $A$ satisfying $R\cup R^{-1}=A\times A$ and $R\cap R^{-1}=I_A$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ है तथा $I_A=\{(a,a):a\in A\}$, $A$ पर तत्समक संबंध है। $A$ पर किसी संबंध $R$ के लिए माना $R^{-1}$ उसका प्रतिलोम संबंध है। तब $A$ पर ऐसे संबंधों $R$ की संख्या, जो $R\cup R^{-1}=A\times A$ तथा $R\cap R^{-1}=I_A$ को संतुष्ट करते हैं, ______ है।
solution: $(a,a)\in R^{-1}\iff(a,a)\in R$, so $R\cap R^{-1}=I_A$ forces $I_A\subseteq R$ (reflexive)
For $a\neq b$: $(a,b),(b,a)$ both in $R$ would put $(a,b)$ in $R\cap R^{-1}$, not allowed (antisymmetric); $R\cup R^{-1}=A\times A$ needs at least one of them
So for each of the $\binom42=6$ pairs $\{a,b\}$ exactly one of $(a,b),(b,a)$ is in $R$: $2$ ways each
solution_full: $(x,y)\in R^{-1}\iff(y,x)\in R$. In particular $(a,a)\in R^{-1}\iff(a,a)\in R$.

Diagonal: $(a,a)\in R\cap R^{-1}\iff(a,a)\in R$. Since $R\cap R^{-1}=I_A$ contains every $(a,a)$, $R$ contains every $(a,a)$, i.e. $R$ is reflexive; the union condition on the diagonal is then also satisfied.
Off the diagonal, take $a\neq b$. $(a,b)\in R\cup R^{-1}$ iff $(a,b)\in R$ or $(b,a)\in R$; $(a,b)\in R\cap R^{-1}$ iff both are in $R$.

$R\cup R^{-1}=A\times A$ requires at least one of $(a,b),(b,a)$ in $R$, and $R\cap R^{-1}=I_A$ (which has no off-diagonal pair) forbids both. So exactly one of them is in $R$ (the relation is reflexive, antisymmetric and any two distinct elements are comparable).
The choices for the $\binom42=6$ unordered pairs are independent, $2$ ways each: $2^{6}=64$ relations.
originality_note: New: relations specified only through their union and intersection with the inverse (universal relation and identity relation), which decodes into reflexive antisymmetric relations with every pair comparable (way 5: algebra of a relation and its inverse linked with counting). Closest known: 'number of reflexive antisymmetric relations on an n-set = 3^(n(n-1)/2)'. Different because: the conditions are given as set identities with R^{-1}, and the union condition removes the third choice per pair, changing 3^6 to 2^6.
blueprint_concepts: Counting reflexive / symmetric / transitive / equivalence relations on a finite set

concept_use.Miscellaneous concepts of Relations: Working with R^{-1}, R u R^{-1} = A x A (universal relation) and R n R^{-1} = I_A (identity relation) to decode the conditions.
concept_use.Counting reflexive / symmetric / transit: The decoded relations are reflexive and antisymmetric with exactly one orientation per pair, counted as 2^6 = 64.
